test_title: PYST 35: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 20 Feb, 2025 - Shift 2)

question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 198 and 33 respectively. If one of the numbers is 99, then find the other number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that the product of two numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF.

Other Number = (LCM × HCF) ÷ Given Number

Other Number = (198 × 33) ÷ 99

Other Number = 198 ÷ 3 = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of the two numbers = 198

HCF of the two numbers = 33

First number = 99

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

**Calculations:**

⇒ 99 × Second Number = 198 × 33

⇒ Second Number = (198 × 33) ÷ 99

⇒ Second Number = 198 × (33 ÷ 99)

⇒ Second Number = 198 × (1 ÷ 3)

⇒ Second Number = 198 ÷ 3

⇒ Second Number = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

The product of any two numbers is always exactly equal to the product of their Least Common Multiple (LCM) and Highest Common Factor (HCF). Note that this rule applies specifically to exactly two numbers.

LCM and HCF of Fractions

To find the LCM of fractions, use the formula: LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators. For the HCF of fractions, use: HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, meaning they share no common positive factor other than 1, their HCF is 1, and their LCM is directly calculated as the product of the two numbers.
